I added `GET /api/admin/users/recently-created`. I didn't run the build or any tests, as you asked.

- **Repository:** `UserRepository` has a new derived query, `findAllByCreatedDateAfter(Instant, Pageable)`. Following `docs/persistence.md`, the service works out the 7-day cutoff and passes it in.
- **Service:** `UserService.getRecentlyCreatedLogins(Pageable)` is read-only and maps the matching users to their logins. It works out the cutoff from an injected `Clock`.
- **Resource:** `UserResource.getRecentlyCreatedUsers` is guarded by `@PreAuthorize` for the admin authority, like the other admin endpoints. It returns the logins as a list with pagination headers.
- **Clock bean:** the project had no `Clock` bean, so I added `config/ClockConfiguration.java` with `Clock.systemUTC()`. `UserService` now takes the `Clock` in its constructor. Nothing in `src` constructs `UserService` by hand, so this shouldn't break any tests.

The endpoint takes a `Pageable` and returns one page of logins, not the full list, because `src/main/java/CLAUDE.md` says list endpoints must be paged. The default page size is 20, so a client has to page through to see every login. Sorting is limited to the same allowed properties as `GET /api/admin/users`.

I didn't run the ast-grep checks.
